content:
emily: Heads-up: CI linkcheck flagged weird 404s on the docusaurus site after the content import. Several anchors with emoji and soft-hyphen characters are generating two different slugs (one from mkdocs, one from docusaurus). Example: 'API — rate limits' vs 'API \u2014 rate limits' ended up with different ids because of unicode normalization.

raj: I saw that too. Also found a stray HTML id on the migration branch where someone left `<h2 id=\"overview-\u00ADbeta\">` (soft-hyphen \u00AD) and docusaurus slugifier drops it differently. Linkcheck shows both /#overview-beta and /#overview-

emily: Repro steps: pull branch, run `yarn docusaurus build`, then `node scripts/link-check.js` to see failing fragments. I posted a short snippet in the PR comments.

tom: I created PR 4421 that applies NFC normalization and strips soft-hyphens before slugify. It also maps common emoji to names (e.g., ':rocket:' -> 'rocket') so anchors don't change when rendered with emoji.

lina: Mapping emoji to names is fine, but be careful: some pages intentionally include emoji in titles for UX. We should preserve a human-readable slug, maybe append the ascii name rather than drop.

docbot: linkcheck: site build (branch/pr/4421) 4 broken anchors detected. Report: https://ci.redwood-inference.local/links/4421/report.html

deploybot: preview: https://deploy-preview-4421.docs.redwood-inference.com/

raj: Small gotcha: PR 4421 changed slug order slightly and caused a couple of intra-doc links to point to the next-heading instead. I added two test fixtures replicating the migration output and flagged them in the PR.

emily: Can we add a lightweight migration script that scans the repo for headings containing non-ascii or control chars and prints suggested canonical slugs so we can reconcile old links? Might help support triage.

tom: I'll add `tools/normalize_headings.py --report` to the PR; it will output a CSV of file,path,old_slug -> new_slug. Also adding a config toggle `enable_unicode_normalization` in the docusaurus plugin.

lina: QA: when testing, clear the node_modules/docusaurus cache and test on both Linux and macos builds. I saw subtle NFC/NFD differences on mac due to filesystem normalizations.

docbot: build: staging/docs (after 4421) 4 broken anchors remaining, mostly in legacy migration pages. Full report: https://ci.redwood-inference.local/builds/7902

emily: Next steps: tom to iterate on the script + flag. raj to run the script against the main branch history to collect common old slugs. We'll decide whether to emit a small redirects.json or update the old pages in-place.

raj: Will run a repo scan and paste results here. If we have fewer than ~50 legacy slugs, redirects.json is easy. If it's hundreds, prefer canonicalization and follow-up redirect rules.

tom: Pushed update: tool now emits a `redirects_snippet.json` and supports a `--dry-run` mode. Also added tests for emoji and soft-hyphen cases.

docbot: build: staging/docs (post-update) 4 broken anchors -> 2 broken anchors. Remaining ones are in third-party imported markdown that still contain literal soft-hyphens.

emily: For those two remaining, we should either edit the source markdown (small vendors) or add two redirects to keep customer links working. I'll open a quick edits PR for the vendor files.

lina: After edits, re-run full linkcheck and then communicate the migration note in the docs changelog. Also ping support to watch for anchor 404 tickets for a week post-deploy.

emily: Thanks everyone. Once staging is green, we'll flip the toggle and run prod linkcheck the next maintenance window.

tom: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4421 (WIP) — please add any test cases you hit.

raj: Scan output (sample): docs/api/limits.md old: api---rate-limits -> new: api-rate-limits, docs/guides/overview.md old: overview-beta -> new: overview-beta

emily: Noted. I'll add a small blurb in the release notes about anchor normalization and a pointer to the redirects map if anyone hits broken links.

docbot: action: tagging @support to monitor for anchor-related tickets during rollout.
